trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Regional Manager - Cape Region: Southern Hub
Company: Old Mutual
About the company: Old Mutual is a firm believer in the African opportunity and our diverse talent reflects this.
Purpose of the role: This is a senior management role in the Cape Region, Southern Hub area, based in Cape Town. The role will manage a branch/area of sales staff comprising about 8 Business Managers. Each Business Manager has a diverse team of approximately 15 financial advisers. The advisers span from new entrants to established financial advisers. The Regional Manager forms part of the Cape Regional EXCO and contributes towards the leadership, direction, and sales strategies for the region.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Meeting area business plan targets including adviser recruitment & retention, sales targets, customer acquisition and market share growth.
  - Working collaboratively with stakeholders within or across areas to optimize synergies and opportunities.
  - Has overall accountability over compliant advice practices, risk management and the operations of the branch under their span of control.
  - Works closely with service and operations support functions to ensure related sales support procedures and standards are adhered to and effectively running to enable sales.
  - Communicate the function's strategy and its relationship to the organization's mission, vision, and values; clarify the actions needed to implement this strategy within the area of responsibility; motivate people to commit to the mission, vision, and values and do extraordinary things to achieve the organization's business goals.
  - Develop a personal network of senior managers within the business sector and at relevant advisory and regulatory bodies. Represent the organization at major business sector events. Obtain market intelligence, promote the organization, and enhance its reputation.
  - Lead a cross-functional internal team (e.g., technical, commercial, and legal) to configure a very complex, high-value tailored or bespoke product-and-services solution and associated contractual terms that meet the customer's strategic goals at an international or global level. Present the solution to customer representatives and negotiate agreement with the customer and internal colleagues to ensure that customer needs are met at an acceptable level of commercial risk, or, alternately, review and authorize complex sales proposals to ensure that they are constructed within acceptable commercial and risk parameters.
  - Ensure quality service and profitable business growth by managing a portfolio of complex customer relationships and/or a small team of account managers.
  - Develop and propose annual business plans for a given area or department, ensuring alignment with strategy. Recommend financial and headcount budgets; propose business targets, for example, revenues or other key performance indicators (KPIs); and schedule key activities/projects, ensuring integration with other elements of the organization.
  - Develop internal marketing plans and work collaboratively with other departments to improve internal relationships in a large organization and to build strong external customer relationships.
  - Develop and implement a relationship management plan for strategic, complex existing accounts to build key relationships at local and national levels. Coordinate the engagement of own organization with the customer organization to ensure effective two-way flow of information and resolution of issues. Manage key client and customer relationships, often through account teams, to ensure their ongoing satisfaction and loyalty.
  - Manage and report on performance within the department or area of responsibility; set appropriate performance objectives for direct reports and hold individuals accountable for achieving them; take appropriate corrective action where necessary to ensure the achievement of annual business objectives.
  - Develop and implement a relationship management plan for strategic, complex potential accounts to build key relationships at local and national levels. Coordinate the engagement of own organization with the customer organization to ensure effective two-way flow of information and resolution of issues.
  - Manage budget plans for a department. May involve development or delivery or both.
  - Evaluate the capabilities of staff within the department to identify gaps and prioritize development activities. Implement the organization's formal development frameworks within the area of responsibility. Coach and mentor others to support the development of the organization's talent pool.
  - Leadership & Strategy: Demonstrate Leadership. Contribute to the development and implementation of the Regional/Area Sales Strategy and monitor area strategy.
  - People Management: Recruitment and Selection. Performance Management.
  - Sales Management: Drive and manage sales growth, viability, and retention for the branch (area). Compliance and business risk management. Stakeholder and partner relationships.
  - Financial Management: Drive business profitability within the branch. Undertake budget and expense management.
  - Operations Management: Drive process and office management efficiencies. Stakeholder and partner relationships.
Must-have requirements:
  - Grade 12
  - FAIS accredited NQF5 (120 credits)
  - Full product holding accreditation
  - 5-10 years managerial experience
  - Managing a sales-driven team or multiple-teams in the financial sector
Nice-to-have:
  - CFP
  - Management and/or coaching qualification
Location: Cape Town
Team notes: Manages a branch/area of sales staff comprising about 8 Business Managers, each with a team of approximately 15 financial advisers. Forms part of the Cape Regional EXCO.
Closing date: 2026-11-09
Employment equity statement: The appointment will be made from the designated group in line with the Employment Equity Plan of Old Mutual South Africa and the specific business unit in question.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Regional Manager - Cape Region: Southern Hub

Old Mutual

Cape Town

About us
Old Mutual is a firm believer in the African opportunity and our diverse talent reflects this.

About the role
This is a senior management role in the Cape Region, Southern Hub area, based in Cape Town. You will lead a branch area of about 8 Business Managers, each supporting roughly 15 financial advisers who range from new entrants to established advisers. You will also sit on the Cape Regional EXCO and help shape the leadership, direction and sales strategies for the region.

Your team
You manage a branch area of about 8 Business Managers, each leading a team of approximately 15 financial advisers. You form part of the Cape Regional EXCO.

What you'll do
• Meet the area business plan targets, covering adviser recruitment and retention, sales targets, customer acquisition and market share growth.
• Take overall accountability for compliant advice practices, risk management and branch operations within your span of control.
• Work with service and operations support functions so that sales support procedures and standards are followed and run effectively.
• Communicate the function's strategy and how it links to the organisation's mission, vision and values, and clarify the actions needed to put it into practice in your area.
• Contribute to the development and implementation of the regional and area sales strategy, and monitor how the strategy is tracking.
• Develop and propose annual business plans for your area, recommend financial and headcount budgets, propose business targets such as revenue and other KPIs, and schedule key activities and projects.
• Manage budget plans and expenses for the department, and drive business profitability within the branch.
• Set performance objectives for direct reports, report on performance, hold people accountable and take corrective action where needed.
• Handle recruitment, selection and performance management for your area.
• Evaluate staff capabilities to identify gaps, prioritise development activities, and coach and mentor others to build the talent pool.
• Lead cross-functional internal teams (for example technical, commercial and legal) to configure complex, high-value tailored solutions and contractual terms, present them to customers and negotiate agreement; or review and authorise complex sales proposals within acceptable commercial and risk parameters.
• Develop and implement relationship management plans for strategic, complex existing and potential accounts, building relationships at local and national levels.
• Manage key client relationships, often through account teams, to support ongoing satisfaction and loyalty, and manage a portfolio of complex customer relationships.
• Develop internal marketing plans and work with other departments to strengthen internal relationships and external customer relationships.
• Build a personal network of senior managers in the business sector and at advisory and regulatory bodies, represent the organisation at major sector events, and gather market intelligence.
• Drive process and office management efficiencies across the branch.

What you need
• Grade 12
• FAIS accredited NQF5 (120 credits)
• Full product holding accreditation
• 5-10 years managerial experience
• Experience managing a sales-driven team or multiple teams in the financial sector

Nice to have
• CFP
• Management and/or coaching qualification

Closing date: 2026-11-09

The appointment will be made from the designated group in line with the Employment Equity Plan of Old Mutual South Africa and the specific business unit in question.
